hpi_details: 44M presents with progressive proximal muscle weakness (difficulty rising from chair), new purple stretch marks on his abdomen, round puffy face, and 12kg weight gain concentrated in the abdomen. Blood pressure checked at home is high.
ideas: thinks he is just getting fat and out of shape
concerns: worried about stroke due to high blood pressure

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Cushing Syndrome is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes using a single guideline-supported screening test for hypercortisolism, confirming abnormal results, then localizing to an adrenal or pituitary source before treatment, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: progressive muscle weakness, facial puffiness, easy bruising, and new hypertension

Key HPI features: 44M presents with progressive proximal muscle weakness (difficulty rising from chair), new purple stretch marks on his abdomen, round puffy face, and 12kg weight gain concentrated in the abdomen. Blood pressure checked at home is high.

Objective/Exam findings: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Cushing Syndrome (hypercortisolism), differential includes adrenal adenoma vs pituitary ACTH tumor.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Cushing Syndrome.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Simple obesity without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: New severe hypertension.
management_principles: Review any exogenous glucocorticoid exposure (oral, inhaled, topical, or injected) as a common mimicker before pursuing endogenous Cushing syndrome workup

Use one guideline-supported initial screening test for hypercortisolism (late-night salivary cortisol, 24-hour urinary free cortisol, or overnight dexamethasone suppression), then confirm abnormal results before determining ACTH-dependent versus ACTH-independent causes
Refer to specialty team and provide comprehensive patient counseling
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

history.answer: My legs have been feeling very weak lately, and my face looks round and swollen.
It is definitely true weakness rather than numbness; I feel like my thighs simply do not have the power to lift me up.
The weakness is mainly in my thighs and upper arms on both sides equally; my hands and feet still work fine.
It started gradually about four or five months ago and has been slowly getting worse week by week.
I really struggle to stand up from a low chair or climb stairs without pulling myself up, though buttoning my shirt is still easy.
It feels consistently weak throughout the entire day, not particularly worse at night or after working at my desk.
No, I do not have any neck pain, lower back pain, or shooting pains going down my legs.
No, my speech is completely normal, my face has not drooped, my vision is fine, and I can swallow without trouble.
No, my bowel and bladder habits are completely normal, and sensation around my bottom is normal.
No, I do not have any shortness of breath, drooping eyelids, double vision, or trouble chewing.
I haven't noticed any twitching under my skin, but my arms and legs seem thinner even while my belly got bigger.
No, I haven't had any recent diarrhea, stomach bugs, colds, or viral infections before this began.
I gained about 12 kilograms over the past six months, but it has all settled right around my belly and upper back while my limbs stayed thin.
Yes, I noticed several wide purple stretch marks appearing on my belly, and I bruise very easily even from tiny bumps.
I checked my blood pressure on a machine at home a few times this week, and it was consistently high around 160 over 100.
No, I have never been diagnosed with high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol, or heart problems in the past.
I have never had stomach surgery, I eat a regular balanced diet with meat, and I don't follow any strict vegan diet.
I do not take any prescribed medications, and I have never taken steroid pills, creams, or joint injections.
I don't do repetitive heavy labor, prolonged squatting, or rest heavily on my elbows during my office work.
I honestly thought I was just getting older, out of shape, and putting on excess weight.
With my blood pressure being so high, I am really terrified that I might suffer a sudden stroke.
I would like to have my hormones checked thoroughly to see if an endocrine problem is causing all these changes.
I have generally been very healthy with no chronic medical conditions diagnosed before now.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I do not take any prescription drugs, over-the-counter pain relievers, herbal tonics, or dietary supplements.
I do not have any known allergies to foods or medications.
I have never smoked cigarettes in my life.
I only drink one or two glasses of beer socially once or twice a month.
I work as an office manager and live comfortably at home with my wife and teenage son.
My father had mild hypertension in his sixties, but there is no family history of strokes, endocrine tumors, or muscle diseases.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is elevated at 162/98 mmHg, pulse regular at 78 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation 98% on room air, and temperature 36.6°C.
Plethoric, rounded moon facies with prominent supraclavicular and dorsocervical fat pads and central truncal adiposity with relatively thin limbs.
Symmetric facial movements, normal extraocular movements without ptosis or diplopia, intact speech, and normal visual fields to confrontation.
Symmetric proximal muscle weakness in bilateral hip flexors and shoulder abductors graded 4/5, with preserved 5/5 strength in distal hands and feet; no fasciculations observed.
Intact light touch, pinprick, and vibration sensation symmetrically in all four extremities without stocking-glove sensory deficit.
Normal 2+ symmetric deep tendon reflexes at biceps, patella, and Achilles; bilateral plantar responses are flexor (negative Babinski).
Thin, fragile skin with scattered ecchymoses on both arms and legs, but no active rashes or ulcerations.
Centrally distended abdomen with multiple broad, violaceous striae measuring greater than one centimeter in width across the lower abdomen and flanks; no abdominal tenderness.
Difficulty standing up from a seated position without pushing off with his hands; gait is otherwise non-ataxic without foot drop.
No cervical or lumbosacral spinal tenderness; negative Spurling test and negative bilateral straight leg raise tests.
